title: Striped hoodie
excerpt: A drop-shoulder hooded pullover in aran yarn worked in bold horizontal stripes. The attached hood is worked by seaming stitches at the neckline and building upward in stripe sequence. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Striped hooded pullovers in aran weight are a popular beginner garment project that introduces hood construction.

glossaryTerms.definition: A row of dc worked into the live neck stitches after the body is assembled. The pick-up row spans the full neckline and forms the base from which the hood is built upward in rows, then seamed at the top.

The seam that closes the top of the hood after the full hood height is reached. The two top edges are aligned and joined with a row of slip stitch through both layers, or a mattress seam depending on the fabric type.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 dc x 16 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran on a 5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 104.3 cm bust.

content.text: Work body and sleeves in 6-row stripes, alternating two colours throughout. Assemble the body and seam shoulders. Work a
across the full neckline. Continue in stripe sequence for 30 cm of hood height, then close the top with a
Size M: 146 sts wide, 81.7 cm body. Sleeve 63.3 cm.
Chain 148. Work 6-row stripes A and B for 81.7 cm. Shape neck on front. Seam shoulders.
Chain 56. Work stripe sequence, increasing each end every 4 rows for 63.3 cm.
Work pick-up row across neckline. Continue in stripe sequence for 30 cm. Fold and seam top.
The two-tone drop-shoulder pullover uses a single bold colour change to create a graphic split across the body.
